title: Flower Colour Census
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: count the flowers of each colour in a garden or park and make a colour chart.

body.heading: Choose your patch
paragraphs: Pick one small patch of garden or park with your adult. Your job is to count every flower colour you can see in that patch — and only that patch.
Scientists who count living things call this a census. You are going to do a census of colours.

body.heading: Count colour by colour
paragraphs: Start with red. Walk slowly and count every red flower, making a little mark on your paper for each one. Then do the same for yellow, white, purple, and pink.
Tiny flowers count too. Look low near the grass, where small flowers like to hide. Bees may be visiting — watch them work, but give them space.

body.heading: Find the winner
paragraphs: Add up your marks. Which colour has the most flowers in your patch? Draw a chart with a bar for each colour to show what you found.
Try the same census in a different patch. Gardens change from place to place and week to week, so your chart is a snapshot of one special day.

takeaway: Counting flowers colour by colour turns a garden into a chart, and shows which colours bloom most in your patch.
materials: A clipboard if you have one
safetyNotes: Count flowers with your eyes — do not pick them, so bees and other people can enjoy them too. Keep a safe distance from bees on flowers.
screenFreeExtension: Make a colour chart picture at home using your counts, with a tall tower of colour for the winner.
